mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 1.0% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 1.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months indicates labor market stress, which compresses wage growth and profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in personal income (PAYEMS) combined with a deceleration in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) indicates a savings-driven shift in household behavior, which can foreshadow lower consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS accelerates and GDPC1 decelerates under the specified thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% combined with a concurrent decline in industrial production below its 12-month average signals a synchronized labor and supply downturn, which increases recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE > 4.5% and INDPRO is below its 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for at least six consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six consecutive months when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.
